result: The authors prospectively identified and isolated neurosphere-initiating cells (NICs) as GEPCOT cells, which represent 3.2±0.7% of SVZ cells. These GEPCOT cells showed high neurosphere-forming capacity (36±6%), with 74% undergoing multilineage differentiation and demonstrating self-renewal potential.
evaluation: Reviewers stated the data are 'extensive, of high quality, use cutting edge approaches, and support the conclusions.' The identification and characterization of GEPCOT cells as NICs is central to the manuscript and was not questioned by reviewers.

result: GEPCOT cells were highly mitotic in vivo, with 35±2% incorporating BrdU after 2 hours and 89±4% after 24 hours, indicating that NICs are highly proliferative and few if any are quiescent.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed the data quality and did not challenge these proliferation findings. The BrdU incorporation data supporting GEPCOT proliferation was accepted as part of the overall high-quality dataset.

result: GEPCOT cells were short-lived in vivo based on fate-mapping with Ascl1CreERT2 and Dlx1CreERT2, with Dlx1CreERT2-expressing NICs persisting less than 7 days and most Ascl1CreERT2-expressing NICs persisting less than 28 days.
evaluation: Reviewers did not question the fate-mapping data demonstrating the short-lived nature of GEPCOT cells. This finding was part of the accepted characterization of NICs versus qNSCs.

result: Pre-GEPCOT cells were identified as quiescent cells expressing higher Glast and lower EGFR/PlexinB2 than GEPCOT cells, comprising 6±3% of SVZ cells, with only 3±3% incorporating BrdU after 24 hours.
evaluation: While reviewers accepted the data quality, they raised concerns about the relatively high frequency (6%) of pre-GEPCOT cells, noting 'it is generally assumed in the field that the quiescent neural stem cells should be a rare population' and requesting further discussion of this heterogeneity issue.

result: Pre-GEPCOT cells could not form neurospheres, with only 1/1663 cells forming neurospheres and only 0.3±0.4% forming adherent colonies.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly noted that 'the authors indicate that they could not grow colonies from the pre-GEPCOT cells under neurosphere conditions or under adherent conditions' but emphasized that 'these cells must proliferate under some conditions, since they repopulate the GEPCOT compartment following its ablation.' They requested data on growth factor requirements, indicating uncertainty about the culture conditions rather than the in vivo properties.

result: Pre-GEPCOT cells expressed stem cell markers (Slc1a3-CreERT, GFAP-CreERT2, Sox2CreERT2, Gli1CreERT2) and were long-lived in vivo, with sustained labeling for at least 60 days, suggesting a long-lived NSC population that replenishes NICs.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed the data quality and conclusions, stating the findings 'make a significant contribution to the field of adult neural stem cells, particularly with regard to the ongoing search for the "true" quiescent adult neural stem cell.' The fate-mapping data was not questioned.

result: GFAP-CreERT2 labeled primarily pre-GEPCOT cells (29±7%) at 2 days, with minimal GEPCOT labeling (6.7±1.9%), and by 28 days labeled cells increased in all populations, demonstrating that pre-GEPCOT cells give rise to NICs, neuroblasts, and other SVZ cells.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge this lineage tracing data. The demonstration that pre-GEPCOT cells give rise to downstream populations was accepted as part of the overall high-quality dataset supporting the hierarchical model.

result: Pre-GEPCOT cells have the morphology and position of type B1 cells (GFAPhigh cells at pinwheel centers with primary cilia), while GEPCOT cells have type C cell morphology (round, unciliated, EGFRhigh).
evaluation: Reviewers did not question the morphological characterization. This data was consistent with prior literature and supported the identification of pre-GEPCOT and GEPCOT cells with known SVZ cell types.

result: Following temozolomide treatment, GEPCOT NICs were ablated (reduced to 10% at 3 days) while pre-GEPCOT cells survived and repopulated the SVZ. Lineage tracing showed regenerating cells arose from pre-GEPCOT markers (Slc1a3-CreERT, GFAP-CreERT2) but not from Ascl1CreERT2-labeled GEPCOTs.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the TMZ ablation and regeneration data. This functional demonstration that pre-GEPCOT cells repopulate the GEPCOT compartment was accepted as strong evidence for the hierarchical relationship between these populations.

result: Conditional deletion of Bmi-1 (Nestin-Cre; Bmi-1fl/fl) depleted both pre-GEPCOT and GEPCOT cells, with pre-GEPCOT cells reduced at 4 months and all populations significantly depleted by 12 months, though some cells persisted for at least a year, demonstrating Bmi-1 is required but not absolutely essential for NSC maintenance.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the Bmi-1 deletion phenotypes. The data showing progressive depletion of both populations was accepted as demonstrating Bmi-1's role in NSC maintenance.

result: Pre-GEPCOT cells were more dependent on Bmi-1 for Cdkn2a (p16Ink4a) repression than GEPCOT cells, with Cdkn2a expression detected in pre-GEPCOT cells from 4/5 Bmi-1-deficient mice at 4 months and 5/5 at 12 months, but rarely in GEPCOT cells.
evaluation: Reviewers asked 'Given the link between p16 and senescence, have the authors ever asked whether senescence is the relevant mechanism for depletion of neural stem cells in their various Bmi1 mouse models?' This indicates the mechanism linking p16 expression to cell depletion requires further investigation.

result: Bmi-1 deletion had no effect on neurogenesis at early timepoints (4 months for Nestin-Cre, 2 weeks for Nestin-CreERT2) but significantly reduced neurogenesis at later timepoints (14 months for Nestin-Cre, 6-12 months for Nestin-CreERT2), affecting all neuronal subtypes examined.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the neurogenesis data. The progressive decline in neurogenesis following Bmi-1 deletion was accepted as consistent with the depletion of stem/progenitor populations.

result: Bmi-1 deletion reduced generation of olfactory bulb astrocytes (at 12 months) and cortical oligodendrocytes (declining at 6 months, undetectable at 12 months).
evaluation: Reviewers noted 'The proportions of new astrocytes and oligodendrocytes that are made from their BrdU-positive proliferating SVZ cells in vivo seem to be very small' and requested comparison of relative proportions, but did not challenge the findings themselves. This is a request for additional analysis rather than a critique of the data.

result: Following inducible Bmi-1 deletion (Nestin-CreERT2), NICs and GEPCOTs were initially unchanged at 2 weeks but Bmi-1-deficient neurospheres were smaller, failed to differentiate, and could not self-renew. By 6-12 months, GEPCOTs were progressively depleted and virtually eliminated by 12 months.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge the inducible deletion data. The progressive depletion of GEPCOTs and loss of neurosphere function was accepted as demonstrating Bmi-1's requirement for NIC maintenance.

result: Following inducible Bmi-1 deletion, pre-GEPCOT cells were not depleted at 2 weeks or 6 months, with a non-significant trend toward reduction at 12 months. Cdkn2a (p16Ink4a) expression was detected in pre-GEPCOT cells from 7/9 mice at 8 months, demonstrating Bmi-1 is required to repress Cdkn2a in pre-GEPCOT qNSCs and that these cells are depleted more slowly than GEPCOT NICs.
evaluation: While reviewers accepted the data quality, they asked about senescence mechanisms (see above), indicating the functional consequences of p16 expression and the mechanism of slower depletion require further investigation.

result: Nestin-Cre; Bmi-1fl/fl mice were smaller than controls but could be aged up to 2 years (unlike germline knockouts). They exhibited neurological deficits (ataxia), relatively normal brain morphology but reduced brain size, smaller cerebellums with thinner molecular layers, and prominent GFAP staining in cortex.
evaluation: Reviewers requested to 'see the enhanced GFAP staining that the authors allude to when they describe the floxed Bmi1;Nestin-Cre mice in Figure 6,' indicating this data should be shown rather than just mentioned. This suggests the characterization is incomplete as presented.

result: Neither Dlx1CreERT2 nor Ascl1CreERT2 labeled significant numbers of pre-GEPCOT cells, indicating GEPCOT NICs do not give rise to pre-GEPCOT qNSCs under steady-state conditions.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge this finding. The lack of labeling of pre-GEPCOT cells by NIC markers was accepted as evidence for a unidirectional hierarchy from qNSCs to NICs.

result: Neurospheres from Nestin-Cre; Bmi-1fl/fl SVZ cells were smaller, unable to undergo multilineage differentiation, and could not be passaged.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these functional deficits in Bmi-1-deficient neurospheres. The data was accepted as demonstrating Bmi-1's requirement for NSC function in culture.

result: Bmi-1 mutant mice showed progressive reductions in BrdU+ SVZ cells (50% at 2 weeks, 90% at 12 months), reduced Mcm2+ and Ki67+ cells, and declining neuroblast populations at 6-12 months.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these proliferation and progenitor data. The progressive decline in proliferating populations was accepted as consistent with stem cell depletion.
